title: Not Open

source.network: Fox News (foxnews.com, World — Fox News Digital, reported from Abu Dhabi)
source.title: Trump meets key Iran war mediator as UAE reveals major oil export surge despite conflict
source.note: published 11-09 13:27 EST; the 11-09 sweep matched it on 'diesel' (strait of), 'iran' and two register keys. Read in full on 11-10 via the cloud fetch (the .print page, complete, 49 body paragraphs) as paragraph reductions, no quotation over ten words. A reported page, not opinion: the author carries the record; two voices of the house (Rubio to reporters Sunday; the holder on 60 Minutes) in paraphrase; the other party (Pezeshkian via Anadolu); four outside readers interviewed at ADIPEC (Hochstein, Wilkinson, Al Nuaimi, Baharoon). Cut 11-10 from the 11-09 sweep (no 11-10 sweep on GitHub at run time) as the RI? corner's full-text row on the live object — the gate at the talks' hinge; chosen over the newer Fox row on Rubio and Vance (15:42 EST, the ticket's split — a bench object) because this page carries the gate, the talks and the barrel's route together; my call, flagged

object.label: H6 — the gate (PG01, proposed 10-15: US control of the Strait of Hormuz), read from the RI? corner six days after the vote at the hinge of the talks: the holder says the Strait is 'open' (60 Minutes, Sunday) while the page's record says otherwise — Reuters' tanker attacks accelerating through October into November, a mine struck east of the Strait Sunday, a former US adviser's 'definition of not open' against CENTCOM's 3,000 escorted transits. Around the gate the talks: Qatar's prime minister at the White House Monday; Rubio 'not on the verge of a breakthrough', Tehran's terms rejected; Pezeshkian ready to negotiate an end to 'neither war nor peace' without surrender; the two-day proposal (lift the blockade and release funds ↔ inspections and the Strait reopened — Axios), not accepted. Beneath both, the barrel's route around the gate: the UAE's exports up from 3.1–3.2 to almost 4.4 million barrels a day via Fujairah, outside the Strait — the hed's 'surge'. The pump and the vote are not on the page; the price is there as insurance, shipping costs and 'consumers far beyond the Middle East'

zAxis.pos: the gate holds and the war closes on US terms — the Strait is open as the holder says, the two-day sequence or something like it is agreed, the blockade lifted for the Strait reopened
zAxis.neg: it does not — the Strait stays a nightly 'hot conflict', the talks stall on terms, the barrel learns to go around the gate and the gate stops mattering as leverage

object.gear: the war itself (the talks, the Strait as a theatre) and the barrel (the route, the throughput, the insurance); nothing on the pump, the vote or the dollar

transformNote: the holder's claim on this page is not the price but the gate: the Strait is 'open' (¶9), said on Sunday as the record on the same page shows tanker attacks accelerating and a mine struck east of the Strait the same day. That is the shadow in its original form — delivery pre-credited where the record does not show it — on the holder's own corner's page, and the page lets three readers answer it: a former US adviser (the 'definition of not open'), Reuters (the attacks), CENTCOM (the escorts, which Hochstein reads as the proof of closure, not opening). What the page does to the object is move the gate from a thing the US holds to a thing the Gulf routes around: the UAE's 4.4 million barrels through Fujairah are the hed's news, and the Emirati readers say the plans predate the war. The talks sit on top — the two-day sequence is the first page on the Press to carry the gate's price in the negotiation as a sequence (blockade and funds for inspections and the Strait)

log.what: daily cut over the 11-09 sweep (no 11-10 sweep on GitHub at 07:00 PT — 404; the newest date in the index, 11-09, used; said so). Forty-nine body paragraphs read in full via the cloud fetch (the .print page); seventeen scored (the hed, the author's ten, the readers' six — all inferred), two constitutive (the holder on 60 Minutes and Rubio to reporters, both in paraphrase). Object declared on H6, the gate, at the talks' hinge: 'open' against the record; the two-day sequence; the barrel's route around the gate. My calls: Rubio @O as the house's voice on the talks (flagged — the Enrollment Ruling has carried the holder and the office @O; a secretary is new); Pezeshkian stationed with the publication (the Baghaei precedent); the readers stationed with the publication (the Sachs precedent); Baharoon's 'third war' on shadow; the Strait and the talks on 'war', the route and the throughput on 'barrel' for the tracked Lumens — the war body's readings are event marks with sigma 0 and the barrel's last reading is 10-30, so both figures are reported, not ruled

split.seam: the gate 'open' (the holder, 60 Minutes; CENTCOM's 3,000 transits) against 'the definition of not open' (Hochstein; Reuters' attacks; the mine Sunday) — on one page in the holder's own corner
split.note: one corner, six scored voices beside the hed and two constitutive. The author: 20 → 24 → 16 → 18 → 14 → 20 → 18 → 16 → 20 → 8 — fluid throughout, the record carried flat; the seam is in what she carries, not in what she says. The readers: Hochstein 36 → 30 → 26 (the verdict first, then the mechanism, then the sizing); Wilkinson 44 (the market lesson — the wrong plane); Al Nuaimi 22 (the number, with one word — 'hostages' — above it); Baharoon 54 → 30 (the blame first, the plans after). Rule 5 across the page: most denominated when a reader names whose war it is ('the third war') or what kind of market the world should have ('resilience'), most fluid at the counts — a fifth, 3,000, 3.1 to 4.4, two days. The shadow is the holder's one line and the page does not contest it in its own voice; it sets the record beside it

lines.quote: 'Trump meets key Iran war mediator'; 'UAE reveals major oil export surge despite conflict'
lines.note: THE DOOR (hed) — the talks and the bypass in one line; the Strait, which the page is about, absent from the door
lines.zWhy: a hed that pairs the mediator with a surge around the gate reads the gate as something to route around, not hold

lines.quote: the holder met Qatar's prime minister Monday at the White House; Rubio: far from a breakthrough; Tehran: willing to negotiate without yielding
lines.note: the record dated — three signals in one paragraph; the mediator's visit the page's occasion
lines.zWhy: a mediator received while both sides say they will not move reads the talks as open, not closing

lines.quote: the Strait 'a major source of global economic disruption'; Gulf governments pushing for a diplomatic solution after thousands of Iranian missile and drone attacks
lines.note: the frame of the page — the gate as the economy's wound and the Gulf's reason to want the war over
lines.zWhy: a Strait that is the economy's disruption is a gate not held

lines.quote: 'I wouldn't say we're on the verge of a breakthrough'; little progress; Tehran's terms rejected; the holder prefers a settlement; Iran's demands unrealistic
lines.note: CONSTITUTIVE — the house on the talks, Sunday, to reporters before Paris (¶3–5 folded); the secretary @O, my call, flagged

lines.quote: ready to negotiate an end to 'neither war nor peace'; 'dialogue and negotiations'; Khamenei has instructed officials to end the uncertainty; no surrender to coercion
lines.note: THE OTHER PARTY — Tehran's counter in its own frame (¶6–8 folded); Dia-scored, stationed with the publication; the first page on the Press to carry the new Supreme Leader's instruction
lines.zWhy: a party instructed to end the uncertainty without surrendering reads a settlement as possible, on its terms

lines.quote: no reason to intensify the war; the Strait of Hormuz is open (60 Minutes, Sunday)
lines.note: CONSTITUTIVE — the holder in paraphrase; THE SHADOW: the gate pre-credited as open on the page whose record says otherwise; later sighting of the 60 Minutes interview (the 11-09 queue's Breaking Points and Shapiro tapes carry it too, transcripts owed)

lines.quote: the two-day proposal: the US lifts the naval blockade and releases some frozen funds; Tehran moves toward renewed inspections and reopens the Strait; broader talks after (Axios); not accepted by Washington; significant differences
lines.note: THE TERMS SIZED — the gate's price in the talks as a sequence, for the first time on the Press (¶10–11 folded); later sighting of the talks' record (fox 11-05: Rezaei's seven demands)
lines.zWhy: a sequence drafted but not accepted is a gate whose price is known and unpaid

lines.quote: the corridor from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman; the EIA: about a fifth of global petroleum liquids and more than a fifth of LNG trade before the war; since: attacks, restrictions, US operations — traffic severely disrupted; attacks continuing despite the naval presence
lines.note: THE STRAIT SIZED — four paragraphs folded; the gate's weight in the world's barrel, dated before the war
lines.zWhy: a fifth of the world's barrel through a corridor still under attack is a gate that has not closed the war

lines.quote: Reuters, Monday: tanker attacks accelerated sharply in October and continued into November; Iran: a tanker struck a mine east of the Strait on Sunday
lines.note: THE RECORD AGAINST 'OPEN' — dated the same day as the holder's claim; the page's most fluid line on the gate
lines.zWhy: attacks accelerating in the month after the gate was declared held read the gate as not held

lines.quote: a 'hot conflict' almost nightly; tankers fired on and hit; a heavy US presence to let one tanker through is the 'definition of not open'; normal navigation not restored
lines.note: THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE — an outside reader refuses the holder's word on the holder's corner's page (¶17–20 folded); the page's title line
lines.zWhy: a strait that needs an escort for every tanker is a gate the war has not opened

lines.quote: higher insurance premiums, the danger of further attacks, restrictions on traffic — the burden on the global economy
lines.note: the price's form on this page — insurance and restriction, not the pump
lines.zWhy: a premium still rising is a gate still priced as closed

lines.quote: CENTCOM, late October: the primary routes cleared of mines; thousands of vessels assisted; a statement reported 10-25 — more than 3,000 transits in six months with US support
lines.note: THE COMMAND'S COUNT — the gate 'open' with a number, set against Hochstein by the author (¶22–23 folded); later sighting of the 10-25 CENTCOM statement
lines.zWhy: a command counting its escorts reads the gate as held by escort — neither open nor closed

lines.quote: escort does not mean the risk has gone; separate tracks — Washington on the 'nuclear front', the Gulf governments on freedom of navigation and the Strait
lines.note: THE PROPOSAL — a mechanism: the gate's negotiation handed to the Gulf states; the two-day sequence read as two tables (¶24–26 folded)
lines.zWhy: a strait negotiated by its neighbours is a gate the holder no longer holds alone

lines.quote: 'Efficiency is not enough. We have to have resilience'; markets built for efficiency; rebalancing security, affordability, sustainability; 'new vulnerabilities of interdependency'
lines.note: the market lesson — the right domain, the wrong plane: the Strait as a case study in market design, not a gate (¶27–30 folded)
lines.zWhy: a world told to rebuild for resilience expects the gate to stay unreliable

lines.quote: the disruption has accelerated the UAE's effort to reduce dependence on the Strait; the pipeline to Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman, outside the Strait, lets some exports bypass it
lines.note: THE BYPASS — the route named (¶31–32 folded); the hed's 'surge' begins here
lines.zWhy: a route built to bypass the gate reads the gate as closed for the foreseeable

lines.quote: exports substantially up since the war began; the UAE wants the Strait open under international law but will not be 'hostages'; 3.1 to 3.2 million barrels a day before 28 February, almost 4.4 now; Al Mazrouei (11-02): at times above prewar
lines.note: THE SURGE SIZED — the number the hed is built on, dated from the war's zero (¶33–36 folded); the barrel's route around the gate counted by the state that built it
lines.zWhy: a state exporting more around the gate than it did through it has stopped waiting for the gate

lines.quote: the UAE and Saudi Arabia anticipated the single-route risk; alternatives are 'redundancies' that reduce the impact but cannot replace the waterway
lines.note: the bypass sized against the gate — a reader's ceiling on the route (¶37–39 folded)
lines.zWhy: a bypass that cannot replace the waterway leaves the gate as the war's object

lines.quote: higher shipping costs and supply disruptions reaching consumers far beyond the Middle East
lines.note: the price's reach — the only line on the page that points toward the pump, without naming it
lines.zWhy: a cost reaching consumers abroad is the war's cost still being paid

lines.quote: 'the third war' — Iran's war on the global economy by blocking the Strait; the Philippines, India, Brazil, with no link to the conflict
lines.note: THE CEILING — the gate's cost addressed to Tehran by an Emirati reader (¶41–42 folded); a line about who is to blame — shadow on the body; the cost's address moved abroad in the other direction from the 11-05 page (Netanyahu)
lines.zWhy: a war named as Iran's war on the economy reads the blockade as Tehran's, not the gate's

lines.quote: single-corridor dependence exposed; 'you will not have only one outlet'; the plans 'have always been there', the war 'accelerated' them; even with Hormuz fully reopened, more routes
lines.note: the bypass as policy, not emergency — the route dated before the war by the reader who argues for it (¶43–48 folded)
lines.zWhy: plans that predate the war and outlast its end treat the gate as permanently unreliable

lines.quote: the White House asked for comment; no response before publication
lines.note: THE HEDGE — the publication's own, and the page's floor; the holder's house silent on its own corner's page
lines.zWhy: a house that does not answer reads neither way
